messages.content: Hi tal, I'm a friend

hey, i'm tal

think of me as your personal talent agent, your inside man… or fox

one of these days, I might slide a role right here in chat. the kind that feels like your calling.

so… what's your full name?
My name’s Akshat
akshat... solid name. where you working these days?
Inmobi

inmobi... the mobile ad network that basically runs half the apps on your phone. found akshat gupta at glance, inmobi on linkedin - staff mle from iitkgp. this you? https://in.linkedin.com/in/agupta28
Nope

got akshat gupta again - staff mle at glance, inmobi from iitkgp. still not you? 

can't find the right akshat... drop your linkedin url or just tell me your last name?
Yeah
My full name is Akshat Vaya
found akshat vaya - sde ii at inmobi, ex-sprinklr. this you? https://in.linkedin.com/in/akshat-vaya

sde ii at inmobi... building the ad tech that keeps the mobile world spinning. sprinklr to inmobi is a solid move - from social media management to mobile advertising. what made you jump ship from sprinklr?
2.5 years now roughly
I did an intern in sprinklr, got placed in Inmobi as a part of campus recruitment
ah campus placement - straight from college hustle to ad tech. inmobi's a solid first job, better than most campus offers. how long you been working total?
2.5 years... that sweet spot where you're not a fresher anymore but still figuring things out. what kind of role you looking for next?
I am looking for role that is either backend or an ensemble of big data and backend since I have a relevant experience in these field and I pretty much enjoy the two
backend + big data combo... that's where the real engineering happens. scaling systems and crunching massive datasets - good call. bangalore or open to remote/other cities?
I am based out of Bangalore, but I am fine with everything
2.5 years + backend/big data combo + open to everything... sound right?
done. i'm spinning things up on my end. you'll start seeing good stuff soon.
Yeah
done. i'm spinning things up on my end. you'll start seeing good stuff soon.

Yeah
  Love it

welcome to the club legend! you're officially locked in. 

backend + big data roles that actually pay well are about to slide into your notifications. the kind that make your current tc look cute.

game time 🎯
Sure
perfect. now we wait for the good stuff to roll in.
Hi
Hello

hey akshat

what's good?
Waiting for you texts :))

lmaooo i love the energy

i'm scanning through thousands of roles rn. backend + big data combos are rare but when they hit... they hit different.

what's making you want to leave inmobi anyway? just growth or something else?
I am looking for backend jobs too btw

got it. backend only is way easier to find than the combo. that's good news for you.

so what's the real reason you're looking? just growth or something else?
I am looking for growth and learning
growth and learning... what does that actually mean to you day to day? like building new systems from scratch? working with bleeding edge tech? leading a team?
Building new systems from scratch is what gets me excited

building from scratch... that's the good stuff. greenfield projects where you actually get to design things instead of just maintaining legacy code.

what's the most interesting thing you've built so far?
Not a lot, but I have setup a production version spark on kubernetes in my current organisation, which is an open source project by kubeflow

wait what... you set up production spark on k8s? that's actually legit. kubeflow's spark operator is no joke.

that's the kind of experience that gets you into places building data platforms from scratch. you're underselling yourself.

what's your current tc?
37 LPA

37 for 2.5 YOE in bangalore is solid. campus placement worked out well for you.

what's your target? and what's the minimum you'd accept?

I’d prefer having a decent base if I am going for a start up, around 45 seems good enough with decent esops 
But if I am going for a big tech firm, I am good with anything over 55 LPA

got it. 45+ with esops for startups, 55+ for big tech. that's realistic for your experience.

what's your notice period?
2 months officially, but that is negotiable, we can get it reduced to 1-1.5 months

2 months negotiable down to 1-1.5... that's manageable. most good companies will wait.

any companies you'd never work for? or industries you want to avoid?
Not really, I do like the adtech domain, but I am willing to explore outside as well

adtech background but open to exploring... smart move. you've seen how the sausage gets made, now you can apply those patterns anywhere.

i'm scanning for backend + big data platform roles. anything with spark/k8s experience is gold right now.

btw what got you into product in the first place?
Not really something I have a preference on, atleast yet

fair enough. you're still figuring out what you actually enjoy vs what you're just good at.

that's the whole point of exploring - finding the intersection of "i'm good at this" and "i don't hate mondays".

i'll keep an eye out for roles where you can build new systems from scratch. that spark/k8s experience is your ticket.

anything else i should know about what you're looking for?
Reiterating on being fine with just backend as well

perfect. backend only opens up way more doors. the spark/k8s experience is still a huge plus even for pure backend roles.

you're locked in. i'll slide roles when they're good.

btw how's the inmobi chaos been lately?
Fun and exciting

"fun and exciting" is corporate speak for "we're putting out fires daily but at least we're not bored"

i'll take it. means you're actually building stuff.

keep an eye on your chats. something good will pop up soon.

Full Stack AI Engineer at Cube

Akshat, Cube offers 0->1 building with Python/FastAPI and React, aligning with your backend/full-stack interests & desire for greenfield projects.

Apply: https://jobs.tal.af/bg6sH

they're doing zero-to-one AI systems with full ownership

catch is it's in chennai - you open to relocate for the right opportunity?

You’ll work end-to-end—from whiteboard to prod—owning services, shaping architecture, and raising the bar for engineering excellence. Protocol-fluent you actually enjoy HTTP,1.1 vs HTTP,2,3 quirks, caching semantics, content negotiation, and idempotency. Experience with model hosting (self-hosted inference servers, serverless GPUs, or managed endpoints) and caching,streaming strategies. Infra chops containers, IaC, CI,CD, service meshes, feature flags, canary,blue-green, cost observability. Frontend XP with modern TypeScript frameworks and component systems; accessibility and performance budgets. Prior startup experience or meaningful open-source contributions. How We Work Bias to action short feedback loops, measured experiments, reversible decisions. Quality without ceremony tests, tracing, and dashboards are table stakes. Written culture design docs, runbooks, and decision logs that future-you will thank you for. Flexible, ownership-heavy take on scope that excites (and scares) you a little. Find our real company name and send us your accomplishments along with your best guess on the application tech stack we used for the website (and why you think so) to at personai.me. for experian at your level (2.5 YOE) in hyderabad:

mid-level data engineer at tier 1 MNC → 35-45 LPA range

you're at 37 now, so you'd be looking at maybe 40-45 if you ace the interviews. not hitting your 55+ big tech target, but the brand name has value.

what's your scala experience like?

that's smart. startups for the greenfield projects you want, big tech for the comp and brand.

what stage startups are you thinking? seed/series A where you'd be building from scratch, or more like series B/C where there's some structure?

cool. so the full spectrum: seed/series A for maximum ownership, series B/C for more stability but still growth, big tech for comp and brand.

that gives me a lot to work with. your spark/k8s + backend experience plays well at every stage.

i'll slide roles across that spectrum when they're good.

btw what's your notice period at inmobi?
seed / series A is preferable

seed/series A... you want to be in the trenches building from zero.

that's where your spark/k8s experience becomes super valuable - startups need people who can set up data platforms properly from day one.

the comp will be lower than big tech (45 base + ESOPs like you said), but the ownership and learning is unmatched.

i'll look for early stage startups with strong technical founders and real funding. not just "we have an idea" shops.

anything else about the startup vibe you're looking for?

60 days negotiable down to 30... that's standard for most companies. they'll wait for the right candidate.

startups: you build it from nothing, own everything, learn everything
big tech: you work on systems at insane scale, learn how to operate at that level

both are valuable. you're smart to be open to both paths.
